The '''2010 [[Tippeligaen]]''' was the 66th completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The competition began on 14 March and ended on 7 November. [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] was the defending champions, having secured their twenty-first [[Norwegian football league champions|league championship]] in 2009.<ref name="Strømsheim">{{cite news|url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2009/09/27/sport/tippeligaen/fotball/rosenborg/erik_hamrn/8258507/|title=- RBK har vært helt overlegne|last=Strømsheim|first=Gro Wold|date=2009-09-27|publisher=[[Dagbladet]]|language=no|access-date=2009-09-27}}</ref> [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]], [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] and [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] entered as the three promoted teams from the [[2009 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]], [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] and [[Lyn Fotball|Lyn]] who were relegated to the [[2010 1. divisjon]].

== Season summary ==
On 6 June, [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]] scored three goals in four minutes and 24 seconds, two of them in [[injury time]], to go from 3–0 down to 3–3 away at [[Molde FK|Molde]].<ref name="Johannessen">{{cite news|url=http://www.tv2sporten.no/fotball/tippeligaen/lillestroem-fra-03-til-33-3223224.html|title=Lillestrøm fra 0–3 til 3–3|last=Johannessen|first=Sturla|date=2010-06-06|publisher=[[TV 2 (Norway)|TV 2]]|language=no|access-date=2010-11-03}}</ref> [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] lost 5–0 away to [[Odd Grenland]] on 26 September. This was their 23rd consecutive top flight match without winning, breaking a record of 22 set by [[Os TF|Os]] in [[1975 Norwegian First Division|1975]].<ref name="Støstad">{{cite news|url=http://www.nrksport.no/fotball/eliteserien/1.7309495|title=Sandefjord med historisk verstenotering|last=Støstad|first=Mads Nyborg|date=2010-09-26|publisher=[[NRK]]|language=no|access-date=2010-11-03| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101002103557/http://www.nrksport.no/fotball/eliteserien/1.7309495| archive-date= 2 October 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> The streak would continue for four matches, ending at 27 before [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] won in their 28th attempt on the last day of the season, beating [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] 6–1 at home. On 31 October, [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] played [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] to a 0–0 draw away, making 2010 the second consecutive season without away losses for Rosenborg.<ref name="Ramfjord">{{cite news|url=http://www.nrk.no/nyheter/distrikt/nrk_trondelag/1.7354045|title=Rosenborg har spilt to år uten bortetap i serien|last=Ramfjord|first=Ole Johan|date=2010-10-26|publisher=[[NRK]]|language=no|access-date=2010-11-03| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101027213826/http://www.nrk.no/nyheter/distrikt/nrk_trondelag/1.7354045| archive-date= 27 October 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

[[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] were relegated at the end of the 2010 Tippeligaen season after finishing in the bottom two places of the league table. Sandefjord ended a two-year tenure at the highest football level of Norway, while Kongsvinger returned to the 1. divisjon after just one season. They were replaced by [[2010 1. divisjon]] champions [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]] and runners-up [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]]. Sogndal returned to the Tippeligaen after a six-year hiatus, while Sarpsborg 08 made its debut at the Norwegian top-level league.

[[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] as 14th-placed Tippeligaen team had to compete in a [[2010 Tippeligaen#Play-off round|relegation/promotion playoff]] with the 1. divisjon teams ranked third through fifth ([[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]], [[Løv-Ham Fotball|Løv-Ham]] and [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]]) for one spot in the 2011 Tippeligaen. This spot was taken by Fredrikstad, who defeated Hønefoss 8–1 on aggregate in the playoff finals and returned to Norway's top flight after just one season. In turn, Hønefoss had to return to the 1. divisjon, also after just one season.

== Teams ==
[[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]] and [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] were promoted directly from the [[2009 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]] at the end of the 2009 season. [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] defeated [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg]] by 5–4 on aggregate in the final matches of the [[2009 Tippeligaen#Play-off round|play-off round]] between the 3rd-, 4th- and 5th-placed team in the 1. divisjon and the 14th-placed team in the Tippeligaen, giving them the sixteenth and final spot.

== Relegation play-offs ==
{{main|2010 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
At the end of the season, [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] and [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] were relegated directly to [[1. divisjon]], and were replaced by [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]] and [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg]] who were directly promoted.

Four teams entered a play-off for the last Tippeligaen spot in the 2011 season. These were:
* A) [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] (by virtue of being the 14th placed team in the Tippeligaen)
* B) [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] (by virtue of being the third placed team in the 1. divisjon)
* C) [[Løv-Ham Fotball|Løv-Ham]] (by virtue of being the fourth placed team in the 1. divisjon)
* D) [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]] (by virtue of being the fifth placed team in the 1. divisjon)
{{#section-h:2010 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs|bracket}}

===Annual awards===
==== Goalkeeper of the Year ====
The Goalkeeper of the Year awarded to {{flagicon|Denmark}} [[Anders Lindegaard]] ([[Aalesunds FK|Aalesunds]])

==== Defender of the Year ====

The Defender of the Year awarded to {{flagicon|NOR}} [[Tom Høgli]] ([[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]])

==== Midfielder of the Year ====
The Midfielder of the Year awarded to {{flagicon|Ghana}} [[Anthony Annan]] ([[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]])

==== Striker of the Year ====

The Striker of the Year awarded to {{flagicon|NOR}} [[Mohammed Abdellaoue]] ([[Vålerenga Fotball|Vålerenga]])

==== Coach of the Year ====

The Coach of the Year awarded to {{flagicon|NOR}} [[Jostein Grindhaug]] ([[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]])
